objects.description: OpenCV exception type carrying error code, message, and source context. Thrown by cv::error and many CV_Assert/CV_Error macros. Use .what() for a formatted description.

Principal Component Analysis utility. Computes eigenvectors/values of covariance, projects data to reduced subspace, and supports serialization. Typical lifecycle: construct, call operator() to compute basis, then project/backProject.
Linear Discriminant Analysis for supervised dimensionality reduction. Offers training via constructor or compute(), and projection/reconstruction. Persists via FileStorage.
Singular Value Decomposition. Decomposes matrices and solves least-squares/under-determined systems. Use flags to control U/V computation. Members u,w,vt store results after decomposition.
Pseudo-random number generator (MWC). Provides scalar generation, uniform/normal distributions, and filling arrays. Thread-local default RNG accessible via cv::theRNG().
Mersenne Twister 19937 RNG alternative. Deterministic with seed(), provides uniform generation and convenient cast operators.
Abstract iterator interface for formatted matrix printing. Used by cv::Formatter implementations to stream formatted chunks.
Factory and interface for pretty-printing Mat objects into various textual formats (MATLAB, CSV, etc.). Use Formatter::get() to obtain an implementation.
Base class for configurable algorithms with IO. Provides common read/write/save mechanisms and static helpers to load objects via FileStorage. Many OpenCV modules derive from it.
Abstract interface for Generalized Hough Transform detectors. Set a template and then detect occurrences in images; parameters expose Canny thresholds, min distance, accumulator resolution, etc.
Concrete Generalized Hough variant (Ballard) for position-only detection without rotation/scale. Configure R-table levels and vote threshold.
Generalized Hough variant (Guil) supporting rotation and scale search. Exposes parameters for angle/scale ranges, steps and thresholds.
Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization interface. Use createCLAHE() to construct, then tune clip limit and tile grid, and call apply().
Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagram builder for 2D points. Supports incremental insertion, queries (locate, nearest), and extracting edges/triangles/voronoi facets.
Interface for LSD line detector. Use createLineSegmentDetector() to instantiate. Provides detection, drawing, and comparison helpers.
Utility to iterate over pixels along a line segment (Bresenham-like). Supports 4/8-connectivity and left-to-right normalization. Dereference returns pixel pointer when bound to an image.
Descriptor for Qt-based text rendering in HighGUI. Obtain via fontQt(), then use addText() to render strings over images or windows.

functions.name: cv::error
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS CV_NORETURN void error(const Exception& exc);
functions.description: Signals a fatal OpenCV error by processing the provided cv::Exception (printing, break-on-error, redirection via redirectError) and then terminating the current flow by throwing/aborting (noreturn). Deprecated overload: kept for compatibility.
requirements: exc must be a valid cv::Exception object with error context fields populated (code, err, func, file, line).
This call never returns; callers must not rely on subsequent statements executing.
Behavior can be altered by prior calls to cv::setBreakOnError() or redirectError().

functions.name: cv::swap
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void swap(cv::Mat& a, cv::Mat& b);
functions.description: Efficiently swaps the contents (headers and, if needed, reference counters) of two cv::Mat objects in-place. Useful to avoid deep copies when exchanging matrices.
requirements: a and b must be valid cv::Mat objects; types and sizes may differ.
Swapping may change which buffer each Mat header refers to; any views/UMat/Mat headers aliasing these Mats will remain referring to their original buffers.

functions.name: cv::swap
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void swap(cv::UMat& a, cv::UMat& b);
functions.description: Efficiently swaps two cv::UMat objects (OpenCL-aware matrices). Avoids data copies.
requirements: a and b must be valid cv::UMat objects; types and sizes may differ.
Underlying OpenCL buffers being swapped may affect sharing with other headers.

functions.name: cv::borderInterpolate
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W int borderInterpolate(int p, int len, int borderType);
functions.description: Maps an out-of-range 0D coordinate p to a valid source index according to the specified border extrapolation mode for arrays of length len. Used internally by filters and copyMakeBorder.
requirements: len must be > 0.
borderType must be a valid cv::BorderTypes value except BORDER_TRANSPARENT and BORDER_ISOLATED for this function.
When borderType == BORDER_CONSTANT, returns -1 for any p; callers must handle -1 accordingly.

functions.name: cv::copyMakeBorder
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void copyMakeBorder(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int top, int bottom, int left, int right, int borderType, const Scalar& value = Scalar());
functions.description: Forms a border around an image/array by copying src into the center of dst and extending edges according to borderType. If src already points to a ROI of dst’s middle, it only fills borders.
requirements: src must be a valid array (Mat/UMat, etc.).
dst must be able to hold type(src) and size(src.cols+left+right, src.rows+top+bottom). It will be created/reallocated as needed.
top, bottom, left, right must be >= 0.
borderType must be one of cv::BorderTypes; if BORDER_CONSTANT, value provides fill color; if using BORDER_ISOLATED, combine via borderType | BORDER_ISOLATED.
When src is a ROI and BORDER_ISOLATED is not set, pixels outside ROI in the parent image may be used for border extrapolation.

functions.name: cv::add
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void add(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray(), int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Per-element saturated addition of two arrays or array and scalar. Supports optional mask and output depth conversion. Multi-channel arrays are processed per-channel.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have the same size and number of channels unless one is a scalar-like InputArray (e.g., cv::Scalar).
dst must have same size and channels as inputs; depth chosen by dtype (-1 keeps input depth when depths match).
If mask is provided, it must be an 8-bit single-channel array of same size as dst; only masked elements are updated.
No saturation if dst depth is CV_32S; overflows may produce unexpected sign.

functions.name: cv::subtract
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void subtract(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray(), int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Per-element saturated subtraction (src1 - src2), supporting scalar-array combinations, optional mask, and output depth control.
requirements: Same size and channels between src1 and src2 unless one is scalar-like.
dst size/channels must match inputs; dtype controls output depth (-1 to infer).
mask, if provided, must be CV_8UC1 and same size as dst.
No saturation if dst depth is CV_32S; overflows may yield negative values.

functions.name: cv::multiply
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void multiply(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, double scale = 1, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Per-element product of two arrays with optional global scale, maskless. Output depth can be specified.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.
dst will match size and channels of inputs; depth controlled by dtype (-1 keeps input depth).
No saturation for CV_32S outputs; overflows may have incorrect sign.

functions.name: cv::divide
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void divide(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, double scale = 1, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Per-element division: dst = saturate((src1*scale)/src2). Supports array/array division. For integer types, division by zero yields zero; for floating-point, IEEE-754 behavior (Inf/NaN).
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.
dst size/type channels match src2; depth may be overridden by dtype. If dtype == -1, allowed only when src1.depth() == src2.depth() for array/array case.
scale is applied to numerator.
No saturation for CV_32S outputs.

functions.name: cv::divide
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void divide(double scale, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Scalar-by-array division: dst = saturate(scale / src2).
requirements: src2 is the denominator array; dst size/channels match src2.
dtype controls output depth; -1 uses src2.depth().
Integer dst: division by zero produces zero; floating-point: IEEE-754 behavior.

functions.name: cv::scaleAdd
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void scaleAdd(InputArray src1, double alpha, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Computes dst = alpha*src1 + src2 per element (classical BLAS SAXPY/DAXPY).
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.
dst has same size and type as src1/src2.

functions.name: cv::addWeighted
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void addWeighted(InputArray src1, double alpha, InputArray src2, double beta, double gamma, OutputArray dst, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Weighted sum: dst = saturate(src1*alpha + src2*beta + gamma). Channels processed independently; optional output depth conversion.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and number of channels.
dst has same size and channels; dtype controls output depth (-1 uses src1.depth() when depths match).
No saturation for CV_32S outputs.

functions.name: cv::convertScaleAbs
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void convertScaleAbs(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, double alpha = 1, double beta = 0);
functions.description: Applies linear transform followed by absolute value and 8-bit saturation: dst = saturate_cast<uchar>(abs(src*alpha + beta)). Per-channel.
requirements: src can be any depth; dst will be 8-bit (CV_8U) with same size and channels as src.
alpha and beta are applied before abs().

functions.name: cv::convertFp16
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void convertFp16(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Converts arrays between 32-bit float (CV_32F) and half-precision floats represented as CV_16S (bitwise FP16). Modes: CV_32F->CV_16S or CV_16S->CV_32F.
requirements: src.type() must be CV_32F or CV_16S; otherwise an error is raised.
dst will be allocated to the corresponding counterpart type with same size/channels.

functions.name: cv::LUT
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void LUT(InputArray src, InputArray lut, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Applies a lookup table (LUT) to an 8-bit input array. For multi-channel src, lut can be single-channel (shared) or match src channels. Handles signed/unsigned 8-bit input via offset of 128 for CV_8S.
requirements: src must be 8-bit (CV_8U or CV_8S).
lut must have length 256 and either 1 channel or same number of channels as src; lut depth defines dst depth.
dst has same size and channels as src, depth equals lut.depth().

functions.name: cv::sum
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_AS(sumElems) cv::Scalar sum(InputArray src);
functions.description: Computes the per-channel sum of all elements in src (1 to 4 channels). Returns a Scalar with sums for up to 4 channels.
requirements: src must have from 1 to 4 channels.

functions.name: cv::countNonZero
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W int countNonZero(InputArray src);
functions.description: Counts non-zero elements in a single-channel array.
requirements: src must be single-channel.
Supported on common integer/float depths; result fits in int for typical sizes.

functions.name: cv::findNonZero
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void findNonZero(InputArray src, OutputArray idx);
functions.description: Collects coordinates of non-zero pixels from a single-channel array into idx as cv::Mat of Points or std::vector<Point>.
requirements: src must be single-channel (binary-like).
idx must be an OutputArray that can hold cv::Point elements (e.g., CV_32SC2 Mat or vector<Point>).

functions.name: cv::mean
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W cv::Scalar mean(InputArray src, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Computes the per-channel mean of src over all elements or only where mask != 0.
requirements: src must have 1 to 4 channels.
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src (ignoring channels).

functions.name: cv::meanStdDev
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void meanStdDev(InputArray src, OutputArray mean, OutputArray stddev, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Computes per-channel mean and standard deviation of src over all elements or masked region. Returns results via OutputArrays (typically 1xN CV_64F).
requirements: src must have 1 to 4 channels.
mean and stddev must be OutputArrays that can accept 1xN CV_64F or similar.
If mask is used, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src.

functions.name: cv::norm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double norm(InputArray src1, int normType = NORM_L2, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Computes the norm of a single array according to normType (L1, L2, INF, etc.), optionally over a mask. Multi-channel inputs are treated as one vector per element with channels combined.
requirements: src1 must be a valid array; Hamming norms only for CV_8U.
If mask is used, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src1.

functions.name: cv::norm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double norm(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, int normType = NORM_L2, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Computes absolute or relative difference norm between two arrays of the same size and type, optionally over a mask.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.
If mask is used, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src1.

functions.name: cv::norm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS double norm(const SparseMat& src, int normType);
functions.description: Computes the norm of a SparseMat (non-zero elements considered).
requirements: src is a valid SparseMat.
normType must be a supported L1/L2/INF type.

functions.name: cv::PSNR
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double PSNR(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, double R = 255.);
functions.description: Computes Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio between two arrays (same size/type). Uses specified maximum signal value R (e.g., 255 for 8-bit).
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.
R should match the maximum representable value for the data depth (e.g., 1.0 for normalized floats).

functions.name: cv::batchDistance
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void batchDistance(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dist, int dtype, OutputArray nidx, int normType = NORM_L2, int K = 0, InputArray mask = noArray(), int update = 0, bool crosscheck = false);
functions.description: Naive batched nearest-neighbor distance computation between sets of vectors. Computes pairwise distances (and optionally neighbor indices) under a specified norm, with options for K-NN, cross-check, and masks.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be matrices of comparable feature dimension.
dtype specifies output distance depth/type (e.g., CV_32F).
If K > 0, computes K nearest neighbors; if K == 0, computes full distance matrix.
nidx is required to receive neighbor indices when K > 0.
mask, if used, constrains comparisons; must be compatible in size.
normType must be compatible with data types (e.g., Hamming for CV_8U).

functions.name: cv::normalize
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void normalize(InputArray src, InputOutputArray dst, double alpha = 1, double beta = 0, int norm_type = NORM_L2, int dtype = -1, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Normalizes an array either by scale/shift to a given norm value (L1, L2, INF) or to a value range [alpha, beta] (NORM_MINMAX). Optional mask restricts computation and modification to a sub-array.
requirements: src is dense array; for NORM_MINMAX, only dense arrays supported.
dst has same size as src; dtype controls output depth (-1 keeps src depth).
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src; computations are over masked region, and only masked elements are modified in dst.
Range normalization is not supported for SparseMat.

functions.name: cv::normalize
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void normalize(const SparseMat& src, SparseMat& dst, double alpha, int normType);
functions.description: Normalizes a SparseMat to the specified norm (L1, L2, INF) scaling so that ||dst|| = alpha. Range mode is not supported for sparse matrices.
requirements: src is a valid SparseMat; only non-zero values are analyzed/transformed.
normType must be NORM_L1, NORM_L2, or NORM_INF.

functions.name: cv::minMaxLoc
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void minMaxLoc(InputArray src, double* minVal, double* maxVal = 0, cv::Point* minLoc = 0, cv::Point* maxLoc = 0, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Finds global minimum and maximum values in a single-channel array, optionally returning their locations and honoring an optional mask.
requirements: src must be single-channel (reshape/split for multi-channel).
minVal/maxVal pointers may be NULL to ignore; corresponding minLoc/maxLoc may also be NULL.
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src.

functions.name: cv::minMaxLoc
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void minMaxLoc(const SparseMat& a, double* minVal, double* maxVal, int* minIdx = 0, int* maxIdx = 0);
functions.description: Finds min and max among non-zero elements of a SparseMat, optionally returning indices (nD).
requirements: a must be a valid SparseMat.
minIdx/maxIdx, if provided, must be arrays of length a.dims.

functions.name: cv::minMaxIdx
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void minMaxIdx(InputArray src, double* minVal, double* maxVal = 0, int* minIdx = 0, int* maxIdx = 0, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Finds global minimum and maximum values in an array and their nD indices. For 2D arrays, indices are (row, col) laid out in an array of length dims.
requirements: src must be single-channel; for SparseMat, only non-zeros are considered.
If minIdx/maxIdx are not NULL, they must point to arrays of length src.dims to receive coordinates.
If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as src; for nD arrays, same shape.

functions.name: cv::reduce
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void reduce(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int dim, int rtype, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Reduces a 2D matrix along rows or columns using sum, average, max, or min. Produces a single row (dim=0) or single column (dim=1).
requirements: src must be 2D. For REDUCE_SUM/REDUCE_AVG, output depth may need to be larger to preserve accuracy; specify dtype if necessary.
rtype must be one of ReduceTypes: REDUCE_SUM, REDUCE_AVG, REDUCE_MAX, REDUCE_MIN.

functions.name: cv::merge
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void merge(const cv::Mat* mv, size_t count, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Merges multiple single-channel Mats into one multi-channel Mat. Each mv[i] contributes its channels in order.
requirements: count > 0; all mv[i] must have the same size and depth.
dst will have number of channels equal to sum of channels across mv (for this overload, typically 1 channel each).

functions.name: cv::merge
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void merge(InputArrayOfArrays mv, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Merges a vector/array of single-channel arrays (Mat/UMat) into one multi-channel array.
requirements: All input arrays must have the same size and depth.
dst will have number of channels equal to the sum of input channels.

functions.name: cv::split
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void split(const Mat& src, Mat* mvbegin);
functions.description: Splits a multi-channel Mat into its component channels, writing them into an array of Mats.
requirements: src must be multi-channel (or single-channel, in which case a copy is produced).
mvbegin must be an array with at least src.channels() elements; target Mats are reallocated as needed.

functions.name: cv::split
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void split(InputArray m, OutputArrayOfArrays mv);
functions.description: Splits a multi-channel array into a vector/array of single-channel arrays.
requirements: m must have N channels; mv will be resized to N and each output array reallocated as needed.

functions.name: cv::mixChannels
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void mixChannels(const Mat* src, size_t nsrcs, Mat* dst, size_t ndsts, const int* fromTo, size_t npairs);
functions.description: Copies selected channels from source matrices to selected channels of destination matrices according to mapping pairs fromTo. Outputs must be pre-allocated.
requirements: All source matrices must have same size and depth.
All destination matrices must be pre-allocated with same size and depth as sources.
fromTo must have 2*npairs entries mapping src-channel index to dst-channel index using continuous channel numbering across arrays.

functions.name: cv::mixChannels
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void mixChannels(InputArrayOfArrays src, InputOutputArrayOfArrays dst, const int* fromTo, size_t npairs);
functions.description: Channel shuffle between arrays (vector-based interface). Destination arrays must be pre-allocated. See mapping semantics in docs.
requirements: All arrays in src must share size and depth; same for dst.
dst arrays must be pre-allocated.
fromTo has length 2*npairs mapping continuous channel indices.

functions.name: cv::mixChannels
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void mixChannels(InputArrayOfArrays src, InputOutputArrayOfArrays dst, const std::vector<int>& fromTo);
functions.description: Same as above, with mapping specified as std::vector<int> of even length.
requirements: Same as other mixChannels overloads; fromTo.size() must be even.

functions.name: cv::extractChannel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void extractChannel(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int coi);
functions.description: Extracts a single channel (coi, 0-based) from a multi-channel array into dst.
requirements: coi must be in [0, src.channels()-1].
dst is reallocated to single-channel with same size and depth as src.

functions.name: cv::insertChannel
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void insertChannel(InputArray src, InputOutputArray dst, int coi);
functions.description: Inserts a single-channel array src into channel index coi of a multi-channel dst.
requirements: dst must be pre-allocated multi-channel with same size and depth as src; coi in [0, dst.channels()-1].
src must be single-channel and same size/depth as dst.

functions.name: cv::flip
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void flip(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flipCode);
functions.description: Flips an array around vertical (flipCode>0), horizontal (flipCode=0), or both axes (flipCode<0).
requirements: src must be 2D; dst will be same size and type.
flipCode controls axis as documented.

functions.name: cv::rotate
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void rotate(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int rotateCode);
functions.description: Rotates an image by multiples of 90 degrees according to RotateFlags.
requirements: src must be 2D; dst type equals src type. Size is same for 180; rows/cols swapped for 90 CW/CCW.
rotateCode must be one of RotateFlags.

functions.name: cv::repeat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void repeat(InputArray src, int ny, int nx, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Tiles src ny times vertically and nx times horizontally into dst.
requirements: ny and nx must be > 0.
dst will be (src.rows*ny, src.cols*nx) with same type as src.

functions.name: cv::repeat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS cv::Mat repeat(const Mat& src, int ny, int nx);
functions.description: Returns a new Mat consisting of tiled copies of src (ny by nx).
requirements: ny and nx must be > 0.

functions.name: cv::hconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void hconcat(const Mat* src, size_t nsrc, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Horizontally concatenates nsrc Mat arrays into one. All inputs must have same number of rows and same depth.
requirements: nsrc > 0; each src[i] must have same rows and depth; channels allowed to vary and are preserved across columns.
dst rows and depth match inputs; cols equal sum of cols.

functions.name: cv::hconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void hconcat(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Horizontally concatenates two arrays with same number of rows and depth.
requirements: src1 and src2 rows and depth must match.

functions.name: cv::hconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void hconcat(InputArrayOfArrays src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Horizontally concatenates a vector of arrays with same number of rows and depth.
requirements: All inputs must share same rows and depth.

functions.name: cv::vconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void vconcat(const Mat* src, size_t nsrc, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Vertically concatenates nsrc Mat arrays into one. All inputs must have same number of cols and depth.
requirements: nsrc > 0; each src[i] must have same cols and depth.
dst cols and depth match inputs; rows equal sum of rows.

functions.name: cv::vconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void vconcat(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Vertically concatenates two arrays with same number of cols and depth.
requirements: src1 and src2 cols and depth must match.

functions.name: cv::vconcat
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void vconcat(InputArrayOfArrays src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Vertically concatenates a vector of arrays sharing same cols and depth.
requirements: All inputs must share same cols and depth.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_and
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_and(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise AND of two arrays or array and scalar, with optional mask.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type unless one is a scalar-like.
mask, if provided, must be CV_8UC1 and same size as dst.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_or
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_or(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise OR of two arrays or array and scalar, with optional mask.
requirements: Same as bitwise_and.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_xor
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_xor(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise XOR of two arrays or array and scalar, with optional mask.
requirements: Same as bitwise_and.

functions.name: cv::bitwise_not
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void bitwise_not(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask = noArray());
functions.description: Per-element bitwise inversion of an array, optionally limited by mask.
requirements: If mask is provided, it must be CV_8UC1 and same size as dst.

functions.name: cv::absdiff
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void absdiff(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element absolute difference between two arrays or array and scalar.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type unless one is scalar-like.
dst has same size and type as inputs. No saturation for CV_32S; overflows may be negative pre-abs.

functions.name: cv::copyTo
functions.signature: void CV_EXPORTS_W copyTo(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray mask);
functions.description: Copies src to dst where mask != 0. If dst has improper size/type, it is reallocated; when reallocated, it is zero-initialized before copying masked elements.
requirements: mask must be same size as src and type CV_8U (1 or multi-channel allowed); non-zero mask elements mark elements to copy.
dst will be created if needed to match src size/type.

functions.name: cv::inRange
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void inRange(InputArray src, InputArray lowerb, InputArray upperb, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Checks whether src elements lie within inclusive bounds [lowerb, upperb] per channel; outputs binary mask (CV_8U). Scalars or arrays accepted for bounds.
requirements: src must be 1-, 2-, ...-channel; lowerb and upperb must be scalars or arrays broadcastable to src channels.
dst is single-channel CV_8U, same size as src.

functions.name: cv::compare
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void compare(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, int cmpop);
functions.description: Per-element comparison (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) between arrays or array and scalar. Outputs CV_8U mask 255 where condition holds.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be single-channel or scalar-like and of the same type/size (except scalar case).
cmpop must be one of cv::CmpTypes.
dst is CV_8U same size as inputs.

functions.name: cv::min
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void min(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element minimum of two arrays or array and scalar.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type unless one is scalar-like.
dst matches size/type of inputs.

functions.name: cv::min
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void min(const Mat& src1, const Mat& src2, Mat& dst);
functions.description: Per-element minimum for Mat overload to disambiguate with std::min.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.

functions.name: cv::min
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void min(const UMat& src1, const UMat& src2, UMat& dst);
functions.description: Per-element minimum for UMat overload.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.

functions.name: cv::max
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void max(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Per-element maximum of two arrays or array and scalar.
requirements: Same as min.

functions.name: cv::max
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void max(const Mat& src1, const Mat& src2, Mat& dst);
functions.description: Per-element maximum for Mat overload.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.

functions.name: cv::max
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void max(const UMat& src1, const UMat& src2, UMat& dst);
functions.description: Per-element maximum for UMat overload.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have same size and type.

functions.name: cv::sqrt
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sqrt(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Element-wise square root for floating-point arrays.
requirements: src must be floating-point (CV_32F/64F).
dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::pow
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void pow(InputArray src, double power, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Raises each element to the given power; for non-integer power, absolute values are used. Specialized fast paths for some powers.
requirements: src can be int/float; dst same size/type as src.
Special values (NaN/Inf) are not handled beyond standard behavior.

functions.name: cv::exp
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void exp(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Element-wise exponent e^{src(i)} for float arrays. Denormals may become zero. NaN/Inf not handled specially.
requirements: src must be floating-point; dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::log
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void log(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Element-wise natural logarithm for float arrays. Output undefined for zero/negative/NaN/Inf inputs.
requirements: src must be floating-point; dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::polarToCart
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void polarToCart(InputArray magnitude, InputArray angle, OutputArray x, OutputArray y, bool angleInDegrees = false);
functions.description: Converts polar coordinates (magnitude, angle) to Cartesian (x,y) element-wise. Angle in radians by default or degrees if angleInDegrees.
requirements: If magnitude is empty, it is treated as 1; otherwise magnitude and angle must have same size/type (floating-point).
x and y will be same size/type as angle.

functions.name: cv::cartToPolar
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void cartToPolar(InputArray x, InputArray y, OutputArray magnitude, OutputArray angle, bool angleInDegrees = false);
functions.description: Computes magnitude and angle for 2D vectors from x and y arrays. Angle in [0,2π) rad or [0,360) deg.
requirements: x and y must have same size/type (float/double).
magnitude has same size/type as x; angle same size/type as x.

functions.name: cv::phase
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void phase(InputArray x, InputArray y, OutputArray angle, bool angleInDegrees = false);
functions.description: Computes only the angle of 2D vectors formed by x and y arrays.
requirements: x and y must have same size/type (float/double).
angle same size/type as x.

functions.name: cv::magnitude
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void magnitude(InputArray x, InputArray y, OutputArray magnitude);
functions.description: Computes magnitude sqrt(x^2 + y^2) of 2D vectors.
requirements: x and y must have same size/type (float/double).
magnitude same size/type as x.

functions.name: cv::checkRange
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W bool checkRange(InputArray a, bool quiet = true, cv::Point* pos = 0, double minVal = -DBL_MAX, double maxVal = DBL_MAX);
functions.description: Checks that all elements of a are finite and, if bounds provided, within [minVal, maxVal). Optionally returns the first offending position.
requirements: a must be a valid array.
If pos is non-null and an out-of-range value is found, its position is stored.

functions.name: cv::patchNaNs
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void patchNaNs(InputOutputArray a, double val = 0);
functions.description: Replaces NaN values in a CV_32F array with the given value.
requirements: a must be CV_32F; it is modified in-place.

functions.name: cv::gemm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void gemm(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, double alpha, InputArray src3, double beta, OutputArray dst, int flags = 0);
functions.description: Generalized matrix multiplication: dst = alpha*op(src1)*op(src2) + beta*op(src3), where ops are optional transpositions/conjugates controlled by flags. Supports real and complex (2-channel) data.
requirements: src1 and src2 must be matrices with compatible sizes; types can be CV_32F/64F or complex CV_32FC2/64FC2.
src3, if provided (non-empty), must match resulting matrix size and type.
flags are cv::GemmFlags (e.g., GEMM_1_T, GEMM_2_T, GEMM_3_T).

functions.name: cv::mulTransposed
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void mulTransposed(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, bool aTa, InputArray delta = noArray(), double scale = 1, int dtype = -1);
functions.description: Computes scale*(src - delta)^T*(src - delta) if aTa=true, else scale*(src - delta)*(src - delta)^T. Useful for covariance computations. Handles repetition of delta if needed.
requirements: src must be single-channel; dtype<0 keeps src depth else CV_32F or CV_64F.
If delta non-empty, type must match output depth; it is broadcast/repeated to src size if needed.

functions.name: cv::transpose
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void transpose(InputArray src, OutputArray dst);
functions.description: Transposes a matrix (no conjugation).
requirements: src is 2D; dst will be transposed size with same type.

functions.name: cv::transform
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void transform(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray m);
functions.description: Applies a linear transform to each N-channel element vector in src using MxN or Mx(N+1) matrix m (affine variant with implicit 1). Commonly used for color space and point transforms.
requirements: src must have 1..4 channels; m.cols must be src.channels() or src.channels()+1; m.rows gives output channels.
dst has same size as src, with channels equal to m.rows; depth preserved.

functions.name: cv::perspectiveTransform
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void perspectiveTransform(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, InputArray m);
functions.description: Transforms each 2D/3D vector in src by a 3x3 or 4x4 projective matrix with homogeneous divide, writing results to dst.
requirements: src must be two- or three-channel float matrix (CV_32F/64F).
m must be 3x3 (2D) or 4x4 (3D) floating-point.
dst same size/type as src.

functions.name: cv::completeSymm
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void completeSymm(InputOutputArray m, bool lowerToUpper = false);
functions.description: Copies the lower (or upper) triangular part of a square matrix to the opposite side to make it symmetric; diagonal remains unchanged.
requirements: m must be a floating-point square matrix.
If lowerToUpper=true, copies lower to upper; else upper to lower.

functions.name: cv::setIdentity
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void setIdentity(InputOutputArray mtx, const Scalar& s = Scalar(1));
functions.description: Sets the diagonal of mtx to the given scalar value (default 1) and off-diagonals to zero (scaled identity).
requirements: mtx must be at least 2D and will be modified in-place.
Non-square matrices get identity on min(rows,cols) diagonal.

functions.name: cv::determinant
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double determinant(InputArray mtx);
functions.description: Computes determinant of a square floating-point matrix. Uses direct method for small sizes (<=3), else LU factorization.
requirements: mtx must be square with type CV_32FC1 or CV_64FC1.

functions.name: cv::trace
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W cv::Scalar trace(InputArray mtx);
functions.description: Returns the sum of the diagonal elements (trace) of a matrix as Scalar.
requirements: mtx must be at least 2D with equal rows/cols for trace to be meaningful; extra channels are summed per channel.

functions.name: cv::invert
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double invert(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags = DECOMP_LU);
functions.description: Computes inverse or pseudo-inverse of src according to flags (LU, SVD, Cholesky). Returns a condition estimate (method-dependent) or 0 if singular for LU/Cholesky.
requirements: src must be floating-point MxN; dst will be NxM with same type.
For DECOMP_CHOLESKY, src must be symmetric positive-definite square matrix.

functions.name: cv::solve
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W bool solve(InputArray src1, InputArray src2, OutputArray dst, int flags = DECOMP_LU);
functions.description: Solves linear systems or least squares: finds X minimizing ||src1*X - src2|| using specified decomposition (LU, QR, SVD, NORMAL). Returns true if a solution (or pseudo-solution) was found.
requirements: src1 and src2 must have compatible dimensions; src1 is coefficient matrix, src2 RHS.
dst receives solution vector/matrix.
For DECOMP_CHOLESKY, src1 must be symmetric positive-definite square.

functions.name: cv::sort
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sort(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags);
functions.description: Sorts each row or column ascending/descending according to SortFlags. Sorts values and outputs sorted copies.
requirements: src must be single-channel; flags must combine SORT_EVERY_ROW or SORT_EVERY_COLUMN with SORT_ASCENDING or SORT_DESCENDING.

functions.name: cv::sortIdx
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void sortIdx(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int flags);
functions.description: Sorts each row or column and outputs indices of sorted order instead of values.
requirements: src must be single-channel; dst is integer array with same size as src.
flags combine dimension and order.

functions.name: cv::solveCubic
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W int solveCubic(InputArray coeffs, OutputArray roots);
functions.description: Solves cubic equation; returns number of real roots (0,1,2). Accepts 3- or 4-element coefficient vector. Outputs real roots (1 or 3 elements).
requirements: coeffs must be 3 or 4 elements (CV_32F/CV_64F).
roots must have capacity for 3 values; only real roots are stored.

functions.name: cv::solvePoly
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W double solvePoly(InputArray coeffs, OutputArray roots, int maxIters = 300);
functions.description: Solves for all complex roots of a polynomial; roots is CV_64FC2 (complex). Returns relative error estimate.
requirements: coeffs is 1D vector of polynomial coefficients.
roots will be complex-valued array with length degree.
maxIters controls iteration budget.

functions.name: cv::eigen
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W bool eigen(InputArray src, OutputArray eigenvalues, OutputArray eigenvectors = noArray());
functions.description: Computes eigenvalues and optionally eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix. Eigenvalues are sorted descending; eigenvectors are row-wise and correspond to eigenvalues.
requirements: src must be CV_32FC1 or CV_64FC1, square, symmetric (src^T==src).
eigenvalues output type matches src; eigenvectors same size/type as src if requested.

functions.name: cv::eigenNonSymmetric
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void eigenNonSymmetric(InputArray src, OutputArray eigenvalues, OutputArray eigenvectors);
functions.description: Computes real eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a non-symmetric square matrix (assuming real eigenvalues).
requirements: src must be CV_32FC1 or CV_64FC1, square.
Outputs types match src.

functions.name: cv::calcCovarMatrix
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS void calcCovarMatrix(const Mat* samples, int nsamples, Mat& covar, Mat& mean, int flags, int ctype = CV_64F);
functions.description: Computes covariance matrix for a set of samples provided as array of Mat, optionally with precomputed or output mean, according to flags (COVAR_*).
requirements: samples must be nsamples elements; shapes consistent according to COVAR_ROWS/COVAR_COLS.
covar will be square; mean Mat is input/output depending on flags.
ctype controls output covar depth (default CV_64F).

functions.name: cv::calcCovarMatrix
functions.signature: CV_EXPORTS_W void calcCovarMatrix(InputArray samples, OutputArray covar, InputOutputArray mean, int flags, int ctype = CV_64F);
functions.description: Computes covariance matrix from a single matrix of samples arranged by rows or columns, as per COVAR_ROWS/COVAR_COLS.
requirements: samples is a matrix with samples in rows or columns consistent with flags.
covar and mean as above; ctype sets covar depth.

functions.name: cv::PCACompute
functions.signature: void PCACompute(cv::InputArray data, cv::InputOutputArray mean, cv::OutputArray eigenvectors, int maxComponents = 0)
functions.description: Runs PCA on the input samples and outputs the mean vector and principal component eigenvectors. Use when you want to retain a fixed number of components.
requirements: data must be samples arranged consistently as rows or columns expected by PCA (see PCA class flags); this wrapper assumes the default DATA_AS_ROW unless you construct PCA differently
mean is optional input/output; if empty (noArray()), it will be computed
maxComponents >= 0; 0 means retain all components
Output eigenvectors will have as many rows as retained components; types follow input type (32F/64F)

functions.name: cv::PCACompute
functions.signature: void PCACompute(cv::InputArray data, cv::InputOutputArray mean, cv::OutputArray eigenvectors, double retainedVariance)
functions.description: Runs PCA retaining enough components to preserve the given fraction of total variance, writing mean and eigenvectors.
requirements: retainedVariance is a fraction in (0,1] indicating variance to keep; at least 2 components are kept by design of PCA class
data layout must be consistent (rows or cols)
mean can be empty to compute from data

functions.name: cv::PCACompute2
functions.signature: void PCACompute(cv::InputArray data, cv::InputOutputArray mean, cv::OutputArray eigenvectors, cv::OutputArray eigenvalues, int maxComponents = 0)
functions.description: PCA with explicit eigenvalues output; retains up to maxComponents.
requirements: maxComponents >= 0
mean can be empty to compute from data
eigenvalues/eigenvectors output sizes match retained components; types are float/double as input

functions.name: cv::PCACompute2
functions.signature: void PCACompute(cv::InputArray data, cv::InputOutputArray mean, cv::OutputArray eigenvectors, cv::OutputArray eigenvalues, double retainedVariance)
functions.description: PCA retaining enough components to meet retainedVariance; outputs both eigenvectors and eigenvalues.
requirements: retainedVariance in (0,1]; at least 2 components are kept
data layout must be consistent (rows or cols)
mean may be empty to be computed

functions.name: cv::PCAProject
functions.signature: void PCAProject(cv::InputArray data, cv::InputArray mean, cv::InputArray eigenvectors, cv::OutputArray result)
functions.description: Projects input vectors into PCA subspace defined by mean and eigenvectors.
requirements: data must have same dimensionality and layout as in PCA training (matching cols/rows to eigenvectors columns)
mean and eigenvectors must come from a compatible PCA model
result will have number of components equal to rows of eigenvectors

functions.name: cv::PCABackProject
functions.signature: void PCABackProject(cv::InputArray data, cv::InputArray mean, cv::InputArray eigenvectors, cv::OutputArray result)
functions.description: Reconstructs vectors from their PCA coefficients back into the original space.
requirements: data must be PCA coefficients with length equal to number of principal components used
mean and eigenvectors must match the PCA model
result will have original dimensionality

functions.name: cv::SVDecomp
functions.signature: void SVDecomp(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray w, cv::OutputArray u, cv::OutputArray vt, int flags = 0)
functions.description: Computes Singular Value Decomposition of a matrix: src = u*diag(w)*vt. flags control computing full/partial U, VT, or only singular values.
requirements: src depth must be CV_32F or CV_64F
flags can include SVD::NO_UV or SVD::FULL_UV
w will be a single-column (or row) vector of singular values; u and vt sizes depend on flags

functions.name: cv::SVBackSubst
functions.signature: void SVBackSubst(cv::InputArray w, cv::InputArray u, cv::InputArray vt, cv::InputArray rhs, cv::OutputArray dst)
functions.description: Solves a linear system using precomputed SVD components: x = VT^T * diag(w)^{-1} * U^T * rhs.
requirements: w, u, vt must come from compatible SVD of the same left-hand matrix
rhs must have compatible number of rows
dst is the solution vector/matrix

functions.name: cv::Mahalanobis
functions.signature: double Mahalanobis(cv::InputArray v1, cv::InputArray v2, cv::InputArray icovar)
functions.description: Computes the Mahalanobis distance between two vectors given the inverse covariance matrix.
requirements: v1 and v2 must be 1D vectors of same length and type
icovar must be square matrix of size matching vector length and be the inverse covariance
Return is non-negative double

functions.name: cv::dft
functions.signature: void dft(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int flags = 0, int nonzeroRows = 0)
functions.description: Computes forward or inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (1D or 2D). flags control direction, scaling, and row-wise transform.
requirements: src can be real or complex floating-point; use CV_32F or CV_64F
For forward real input without DFT_COMPLEX_OUTPUT, result is packed CCS format; else complex
If DFT_INVERSE is set, optionally set DFT_SCALE to normalize the inverse
nonzeroRows can optimize when only top rows contain non-zeros
Arrays should have sizes factorable by small primes for performance

functions.name: cv::idft
functions.signature: void idft(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int flags = 0, int nonzeroRows = 0)
functions.description: Inverse DFT convenience wrapper equivalent to dft(src,dst,flags|DFT_INVERSE,nonzeroRows).
requirements: Same type and layout constraints as dft
DFT_SCALE not automatically set; specify if you need normalized inverse

functions.name: cv::dct
functions.signature: void dct(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int flags = 0)
functions.description: Computes forward or inverse Discrete Cosine Transform (1D/2D).
requirements: src must be floating-point (CV_32F or CV_64F)
flags may include DCT_INVERSE and DCT_ROWS
Even-size vectors/matrices are supported; performance depends on size

functions.name: cv::idct
functions.signature: void idct(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int flags = 0)
functions.description: Inverse DCT convenience wrapper: dct(src,dst,flags|DCT_INVERSE).
requirements: Same requirements as dct

functions.name: cv::mulSpectrums
functions.signature: void mulSpectrums(cv::InputArray a, cv::InputArray b, cv::OutputArray c, int flags, bool conjB = false)
functions.description: Per-element multiplication of two Fourier spectra (complex or CCS-packed). Used for convolution/correlation in frequency domain.
requirements: a and b must have same size and type, complex/CCS-compatible with dft outputs
flags may include DFT_ROWS for row-wise processing
Set conjB=true for correlation-like multiplication
Output c has same size/type as inputs

functions.name: cv::getOptimalDFTSize
functions.signature: int getOptimalDFTSize(int vecsize)
functions.description: Returns minimal N >= vecsize such that N is fast for DFT (product of 2,3,5).
requirements: vecsize must be non-negative and not extremely close to INT_MAX
Return may be negative if vecsize too large

functions.name: cv::theRNG
functions.signature: cv::RNG& theRNG()
functions.description: Returns thread-local default random number generator object for generating random values efficiently in tight loops.
requirements: RNG object is valid per-thread; use directly for repeated draws (e.g., rng() or rng.uniform)
Use setRNGSeed to reseed global RNG state

functions.name: cv::setRNGSeed
functions.signature: void setRNGSeed(int seed)
functions.description: Sets the seed of the default RNG returned by theRNG().
requirements: Call affects the calling thread's default RNG state
seed is 32-bit integer; seed=0 will still initialize to default non-zero state by RNG constructor semantics

functions.name: cv::randu
functions.signature: void randu(cv::InputOutputArray dst, cv::InputArray low, cv::InputArray high)
functions.description: Fills dst with uniformly distributed random numbers in [low, high).
requirements: dst must be pre-allocated; 1–4 channels supported
low/high can be scalars or arrays broadcastable per channel; types must be compatible with dst
For integer dst, range is clamped/saturated to dst type
For floating dst, exact uniform in [low, high)

functions.name: cv::randn
functions.signature: void randn(cv::InputOutputArray dst, cv::InputArray mean, cv::InputArray stddev)
functions.description: Fills dst with normally distributed random numbers with given mean and standard deviation.
requirements: dst must be pre-allocated; 1–4 channels supported
mean and stddev can be vectors (diagonal covariance) or matrices; broadcast per channel
Values are clipped to dst data type range

functions.name: cv::randShuffle
functions.signature: void randShuffle(cv::InputOutputArray dst, double iterFactor = 1., cv::RNG* rng = 0)
functions.description: Randomly shuffles 1D array elements using swaps; number of swaps ~ rows*cols*iterFactor.
requirements: dst must be a numerical 1D array (treats Mat as flat)
iterFactor >= 0; higher values mean more thorough shuffling
If rng is null, uses theRNG()

functions.name: cv::kmeans
functions.signature: double kmeans(cv::InputArray data, int K, cv::InputOutputArray bestLabels, cv::TermCriteria criteria, int attempts, int flags, cv::OutputArray centers = cv::noArray())
functions.description: k-means clustering: partitions data into K clusters; outputs labels and cluster centers; returns compactness (sum of squared distances).
requirements: data must be N samples in floating-point (rows or single-channel points as documented)
bestLabels must be CV_32S vector of length N; when flags includes KMEANS_USE_INITIAL_LABELS, it must be initialized
criteria defines termination (max iterations and/or epsilon)
attempts >= 1; the best (lowest compactness) among attempts is chosen
flags must be one of KmeansFlags for center initialization
centers if provided will be KxDims float matrix

functions.name: cv::Formatter::get
functions.signature: static cv::Ptr<cv::Formatter> cv::Formatter::get(cv::Formatter::FormatType fmt = cv::Formatter::FMT_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Factory to get a formatter for pretty-printing cv::Mat and related types in various syntaxes (default, MATLAB, CSV, Python, NumPy, C).
requirements: fmt must be one of Formatter::FormatType enum values

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::write
functions.signature: void cv::Algorithm::write(const cv::Ptr<cv::FileStorage>& fs, const cv::String& name = cv::String()) const
functions.description: Simplified API to serialize algorithm parameters to a FileStorage opened by the caller, optionally under a given node name.
requirements: Derived classes should implement Algorithm::write(FileStorage&) to serialize parameters
fs must be a valid FileStorage pointer opened for writing

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::read
functions.signature: virtual void cv::Algorithm::read(const cv::FileNode& fn)
functions.description: Virtual method to deserialize algorithm parameters from a FileNode. Derived classes override this.
requirements: fn must be a valid node containing the algorithm parameters schema expected by the derived class

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::empty
functions.signature: virtual bool cv::Algorithm::empty() const
functions.description: Indicates whether the algorithm instance is empty/uninitialized (e.g., after unsuccessful read).
requirements: Derived classes should override to signal readiness/state

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::save
functions.signature: virtual void cv::Algorithm::save(const cv::String& filename) const
functions.description: Saves the algorithm to a file by opening a FileStorage and delegating to write().
requirements: Derived class must implement write(FileStorage&) to actually save
filename must be writable path

functions.name: cv::Algorithm::getDefaultName
functions.signature: virtual cv::String cv::Algorithm::getDefaultName() const
functions.description: Returns default string identifier used as top-level XML/YAML node when saving.
requirements: Derived classes may override to customize node name

functions.name: cv::getGaussianKernel
functions.signature: cv::Mat getGaussianKernel(int ksize, double sigma, int ktype = CV_64F)
functions.description: Generates a 1D Gaussian kernel of length ksize and standard deviation sigma, normalized to sum to 1.
requirements: ksize must be positive odd
sigma > 0 or if <=0, computed from ksize via heuristic
ktype must be CV_32F or CV_64F

functions.name: cv::getDerivKernels
functions.signature: void getDerivKernels(cv::OutputArray kx, cv::OutputArray ky, int dx, int dy, int ksize, bool normalize = false, int ktype = CV_32F)
functions.description: Computes 1D derivative kernels (Sobel/Scharr) for orders dx,dy and aperture size.
requirements: ksize must be FILTER_SCHARR (-1), 1, 3, 5, or 7
dx, dy are derivative orders; for ksize=1 only first/second derivatives allowed
If normalize=true, kernels scaled to preserve fractional bits; for floating-point images normalization usually desired
ktype must be CV_32F or CV_64F

functions.name: cv::getGaborKernel
functions.signature: cv::Mat getGaborKernel(cv::Size ksize, double sigma, double theta, double lambd, double gamma, double psi = CV_PI*0.5, int ktype = CV_64F)
functions.description: Creates a 2D Gabor filter kernel with specified parameters (Gaussian envelope and sinusoidal carrier).
requirements: ksize width/height > 0
sigma > 0; lambd (wavelength) > 0; gamma > 0
theta, psi in radians
ktype CV_32F or CV_64F

functions.name: cv::getStructuringElement
functions.signature: cv::Mat getStructuringElement(int shape, cv::Size ksize, cv::Point anchor = cv::Point(-1,-1))
functions.description: Builds a binary structuring element for morphology (rect, cross, ellipse) of given size and anchor.
requirements: shape one of MorphShapes
ksize width and height > 0
anchor default (-1,-1) means center; only cross shape depends on anchor position

functions.name: cv::medianBlur
functions.signature: void medianBlur(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int ksize)
functions.description: Applies median filtering with ksize x ksize aperture, per channel, to remove impulsive noise.
requirements: ksize must be odd and > 1 (e.g., 3,5,7,...)
For ksize 3 or 5, src depth can be CV_8U, CV_16U, or CV_32F; for larger ksize only CV_8U
dst same size and type as src

functions.name: cv::GaussianBlur
functions.signature: void GaussianBlur(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, cv::Size ksize, double sigmaX, double sigmaY = 0, int borderType = cv::BORDER_DEFAULT)

requirements: ddepth = -1 to keep or specify target depth
ksize width/height > 0
BORDER_WRAP not supported

ksize width/height > 0

functions.name: cv::filter2D

ddepth = -1 to keep or specify target depth

functions.signature: void sepFilter2D(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int ddepth, cv::InputArray kernelX, cv::InputArray kernelY, cv::Point anchor = cv::Point(-1,-1), double delta = 0, int borderType = cv::BORDER_DEFAULT)

ddepth = -1 to keep or specify target depth
BORDER_WRAP not supported

functions.description: Computes image derivatives using Sobel (or Scharr when ksize=-1) operator of order (dx,dy).

ksize in {1,3,5,7} or FILTER_SCHARR (-1)

functions.signature: void spatialGradient(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dx, cv::OutputArray dy, int ksize = 3, int borderType = cv::BORDER_DEFAULT)

requirements: ksize must be 3 (per docs)
borderType must be BORDER_DEFAULT (REFLECT_101) or BORDER_REPLICATE

functions.name: cv::Scharr
functions.signature: void Scharr(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int ddepth, int dx, int dy, double scale = 1, double delta = 0, int borderType = cv::BORDER_DEFAULT)

functions.signature: void Laplacian(cv::InputArray src, cv::OutputArray dst, int ddepth, int ksize = 1, double scale = 1, double delta = 0, int borderType = cv::BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes the Laplacian (sum of second derivatives) using Sobel kernels of size ksize or a fixed 3x3 if ksize==1.

ksize must be positive odd; 1 uses 3x3 fixed kernel
BORDER_WRAP not supported

functions.signature: void Canny(cv::InputArray image, cv::OutputArray edges, double threshold1, double threshold2, int apertureSize = 3, bool L2gradient = false)
functions.description: Canny edge detector from grayscale input using internally computed gradients.

apertureSize is Sobel aperture (odd, 3..7)
threshold1 <= threshold2 typically; choose according to hysteresis

functions.name: cv::Canny
functions.signature: void Canny(cv::InputArray dx, cv::InputArray dy, cv::OutputArray edges, double threshold1, double threshold2, bool L2gradient = false)
functions.description: Canny edge detector using precomputed derivatives dx,dy.

thresholds and L2gradient semantics same as other overload

functions.name: cv::cornerMinEigenVal
functions.signature: void cv::cornerMinEigenVal(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int blockSize, int ksize = 3, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes the minimal eigenvalue of the 2x2 gradient covariance matrix in a neighborhood for each pixel. Use for corner strength maps prior to corner detection. Returns a CV_32FC1 map in dst.
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point image.
dst will be same size as src and type CV_32FC1.
blockSize is the neighborhood size; positive integer.
ksize is Sobel aperture size; typically 3; integer.
borderType must be a valid BorderTypes; BORDER_WRAP not supported.

functions.name: cv::cornerHarris
functions.signature: void cv::cornerHarris(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int blockSize, int ksize, double k, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes the Harris corner measure for each pixel from local gradient covariance. Produces a CV_32FC1 response map for corner detection.
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point image.
dst same size as src; type CV_32FC1.
blockSize positive neighborhood size.
ksize Sobel aperture size; integer.
k Harris free parameter (double).
borderType must be a valid BorderTypes; BORDER_WRAP not supported.

functions.name: cv::cornerEigenValsAndVecs
functions.signature: void cv::cornerEigenValsAndVecs(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int blockSize, int ksize, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: For each pixel computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the local 2x2 gradient covariance matrix. Stores per-pixel 6-float vector (λ1, λ2, x1, y1, x2, y2).
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point image.
dst has same size as src and type CV_32FC(6).
blockSize positive; ksize Sobel aperture.
borderType valid; BORDER_WRAP not supported.

functions.name: cv::preCornerDetect
functions.signature: void cv::preCornerDetect(InputArray src, OutputArray dst, int ksize, int borderType = BORDER_DEFAULT)
functions.description: Computes a derivative-based cornerness map used before corner localization. Outputs CV_32F image with higher values near corner-like structures.
requirements: src must be single-channel 8-bit or floating-point.
dst same size as src; type CV_32F.
ksize Sobel aperture (odd).
borderType valid; BORDER_WRAP not supported.

functions.name: cv::cornerSubPix
functions.signature: void cv::cornerSubPix(InputArray image, InputOutputArray corners, Size winSize, Size zeroZone, TermCriteria criteria)
functions.description: Refines corner (or saddle) positions to sub-pixel accuracy using iterative optimization in a search window around each initial point.
requirements: image must be single-channel 8-bit or float.
corners must contain initial points; refined in-place; shape Nx1/CV_32FC2 or equivalent.
winSize specifies half window size; positive ints.
zeroZone either (-1,-1) or small non-negative to avoid center region.
criteria defines termination (max iterations and/or epsilon).

functions.name: cv::goodFeaturesToTrack
functions.signature: void cv::goodFeaturesToTrack(InputArray image, OutputArray corners, int maxCorners, double qualityLevel, double minDistance, InputArray mask = noArray(), int blockSize = 3, bool useHarrisDetector = false, double k = 0.04)
functions.description: Detects up to maxCorners strongest corners in a grayscale image using Shi-Tomasi (default) or Harris measure with non-maximum suppression and distance filtering.

corners receives Nx1 CV_32FC2 points.
maxCorners > 0 to limit count; <=0 means no limit.
qualityLevel in (0,1]; multiplied by max response to threshold.
minDistance minimal Euclidean spacing between returned corners (pixels).
mask optional 8U single-channel same size as image; non-zero marks valid region.
blockSize neighborhood for covariance matrix.
If useHarrisDetector=true, k is Harris parameter.

functions.name: cv::goodFeaturesToTrack
functions.signature: void cv::goodFeaturesToTrack(InputArray image, OutputArray corners, int maxCorners, double qualityLevel, double minDistance, InputArray mask, int blockSize, int gradientSize, bool useHarrisDetector = false, double k = 0.04)
functions.description: Overload adding explicit Sobel gradient aperture size (gradientSize).
requirements: Same as other overload plus: gradientSize is Sobel aperture size; odd.
image, mask constraints as above.

functions.name: cv::goodFeaturesToTrackWithQuality
functions.signature: void cv::goodFeaturesToTrack(InputArray image, OutputArray corners, int maxCorners, double qualityLevel, double minDistance, InputArray mask, OutputArray cornersQuality, int blockSize = 3, int gradientSize = 3, bool useHarrisDetector = false, double k = 0.04)
functions.description: Variant that also returns per-corner quality measure values via cornersQuality.
requirements: Same input constraints as goodFeaturesToTrack.
cornersQuality will be output vector (CV_32F) matching corners count.

functions.name: cv::HoughLines
functions.signature: void cv::HoughLines(InputArray image, OutputArray lines, double rho, double theta, int threshold, double srn = 0, double stn = 0, double min_theta = 0, double max_theta = CV_PI)
functions.description: Detects lines using standard or multi-scale Hough transform on a binary edge image. Returns (rho, theta) or (rho, theta, votes).

theta>0 (angle resolution in radians).
threshold positive votes threshold.

min_theta/max_theta define search angle range within [0, PI].

functions.name: cv::HoughLinesP
functions.signature: void cv::HoughLinesP(InputArray image, OutputArray lines, double rho, double theta, int threshold, double minLineLength = 0, double maxLineGap = 0)
functions.description: Detects line segments using probabilistic Hough transform. Returns (x1,y1,x2,y2) per line.
requirements: image must be 8-bit single-channel binary edge map.
lines output CV_32SC4 or CV_32FC4; size Nx1.
rho, theta, threshold as in HoughLines.
minLineLength non-negative; segments shorter are rejected.
maxLineGap non-negative; maximum gap to link points.

functions.name: cv::HoughLinesPointSet
functions.signature: void cv::HoughLinesPointSet(InputArray point, OutputArray lines, int lines_max, int threshold, double min_rho, double max_rho, double rho_step, double min_theta, double max_theta, double theta_step)
functions.description: Detects lines from a set of points using modified Hough transform. Returns (votes, rho, theta) for up to lines_max lines.

lines_max > 0; threshold > 0.
min_rho < max_rho, rho_step > 0.
min_theta < max_theta within [0, PI], theta_step > 0.

functions.name: cv::HoughCircles
functions.signature: void cv::HoughCircles(InputArray image, OutputArray circles, int method, double dp, double minDist, double param1 = 100, double param2 = 100, int minRadius = 0, int maxRadius = 0)

method is cv::HoughModes: HOUGH_GRADIENT or HOUGH_GRADIENT_ALT.

minRadius >= 0; maxRadius >= 0; if maxRadius<=0 special handling as docs.

functions.name: cv::erode

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: generic string
# Used by fuzzer stub as the node name for FileStorage when writing Algorithm (CLAHE) parameters.
# OpenCV FileStorage node names are best kept as reasonable ASCII identifiers without YAML special chars
# to ensure consistent serialization. We'll generate a variety of names:
# - simple alphanumerics
# - names with namespaces/paths-like separators
# - names with Unicode letters
# - edge cases: empty, very long, starting with digit/underscore, containing dots/colons
# The function returns bytes suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_STR initial buffer.

MAX_LEN = 256

_ascii = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
_sep = ["/", ":", ".", "::"]

_unicode_chunks = [
    "Αλφα",      # Greek
    "данные",    # Cyrillic
    "数据",        # CJK
    "नाम",        # Devanagari
    "éçà",        # Latin accents
]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(_ascii) for _ in range(n))


def _with_separators(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = [
        _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8),
        _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6),
        _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 10),
    ]
    # Randomly insert different separators
    name = parts[0]
    for p in parts[1:]:
        sep = rng.choice(_sep)
        name += sep + p
    return name


def _with_unicode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)
    uni = rng.choice(_unicode_chunks)
    tail = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 6)
    return base + "_" + uni + ("_" + tail if tail else "")


def _very_long(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a long but reasonable node name by repeating segments with separators
    segments: List[str] = []
    total = 0
    while total < MAX_LEN - 1:
        seg = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12)
        sep = rng.choice(["/", ":", ".", "-"])
        chunk = (sep if segments else "") + seg
        if total + len(chunk) > MAX_LEN:
            break
        segments.append(chunk)
        total += len(chunk)
    return "".join(segments)


def _edge_case(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    cases = [
        "",  # empty
        "_",  # single underscore
        ".",  # single dot
        ":",  # single colon
        "0",  # leading digit
        "name",  # simple
        "node.name",  # dotted
        "ns::Class",  # C++-like
        "cfg/profile:default",  # path-like with colon
    ]
    return rng.choice(cases)


def _candidate_names(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    names = []
    names.append(_edge_case(rng))
    names.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 20))
    names.append(_with_separators(rng))
    names.append(_with_unicode(rng))
    names.append(_very_long(rng))
    # Ensure uniqueness and non-None
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for n in names:
        if n not in seen:
            seen.add(n)
            uniq.append(n)
    return uniq


def _serialize_choice(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> bytes:
    # Return UTF-8 bytes; FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumes bytes as string
    return s.encode('utf-8')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    names = _candidate_names(rng)
    choice = rng.choice(names)
    # Occasionally trim or pad with benign characters to vary length
    mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 1 and len(choice) > 0:
        # slice from random start to end to create shorter substrings
        start = rng.randrange(0, min(len(choice), 5))
        choice = choice[start:]
    elif mode == 2:
        # append a small suffix
        choice += rng.choice(["", "_v1", ".yml", ":node", "/sub"]) 
    # Enforce max length
    if len(choice) > MAX_LEN:
        choice = choice[:MAX_LEN]
    return _serialize_choice(rng, choice)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() as a writable path for Algorithm::save
# Goal: generate plausible, writable file paths with varied characteristics, within 4096 bytes
# Constraints: no I/O. Return bytes. Seeded randomness.

MAX_LEN = 256

def _random_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Include varied chars: ascii letters, digits, some safe punctuation, unicode subset
    safe = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."
    # Add a few unicode letters to exercise UTF-8 paths
    unicode_opts = [
        "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß", "é", "日本", "文件", "данные", "फ़ाइल",
    ]
    name_len = rng.randint(1, 32)
    name = ''.join(rng.choice(safe) for _ in range(name_len)).strip()
    # Ensure not empty after strip
    if not name:
        name = "tmp"
    # Occasionally inject unicode tokens
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        token = rng.choice(unicode_opts)
        insert_pos = rng.randint(0, len(name))
        name = name[:insert_pos] + token + name[insert_pos:]
    # Avoid reserved names on Windows
    reserved = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL"} | {f"COM{i}" for i in range(1,10)} | {f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1,10)}
    if name.upper().split('.')[0] in reserved:
        name = "file_" + name
    # Avoid trailing dots/spaces on Windows
    name = name.rstrip(' .') or "file"
    return name

def _random_extension(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    exts = [".xml", ".yml", ".yaml", ".json", ".bin", ".dat", ".txt", ".cfg"]
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        return rng.choice(exts)
    # randomly craft extension
    ext_len = rng.randint(1, 4)
    ext_chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits
    return "." + ''.join(rng.choice(ext_chars) for _ in range(ext_len))

def _random_dirs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    parts = []
    # Depth 0..3
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        part = _random_basename(rng)
        # Sanitize separators and illegal characters minimally
        part = part.replace(os.sep, "-")
        if os.altsep:
            part = part.replace(os.altsep, "-")
        parts.append(part)
    return parts

def _maybe_temp_root(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a root likely writable in typical fuzz envs
    # Prefer current directory or tmp variants
    choices = [".", "./out", "./build", "./tmp", "./.cache"]
    # On Unix, also try /tmp; on Windows, try .\\tmp style
    if os.name == 'nt':
        choices += [".\\", ".\\tmp", ".\\out", ".\\build"]
    else:
        choices += ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/dev/shm"]
    # Bias towards relative paths for portability
    weights = [5, 3, 2, 4, 2] + [1]* (len(choices)-5)
    # Normalize weights
    if len(weights) != len(choices):
        weights = [1]*len(choices)
    return rng.choices(choices, weights=weights, k=1)[0]

def _compose_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    root = _maybe_temp_root(rng)
    dirs = _random_dirs(rng)
    base = _random_basename(rng)
    # Occasionally create nested directories ending with dotfiles or long names
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        dirs.append("." + base[: max(1, len(base)//2)])
        base = _random_basename(rng)
    # Add extension
    base += _random_extension(rng)

    # Join respecting OS
    # If root looks like absolute (starts with / or drive), use as root, else treat as relative
    parts = []
    if root.startswith("/") or (os.name == 'nt' and (root.startswith(".\\") or root.startswith("\\") or (len(root) >= 2 and root[1] == ':'))):
        # Keep root as prefix string
        prefix = root
    else:
        prefix = root
    path = prefix
    for d in dirs:
        path = os.path.join(path, d)
    path = os.path.join(path, base)

    # Optionally add unusual traits: spaces, multiple dots, long segment
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        path = path.replace(" ", "_")  # reduce spaces sometimes
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # add version-like suffix before extension
        name, ext = os.path.splitext(path)
        path = f"{name}.v{rng.randint(0,99)}{ext}"

    # Truncate to max length
    if len(path) > MAX_LEN:
        name, ext = os.path.splitext(path)
        keep = MAX_LEN - len(ext) - 1
        path = (name[:keep] if keep > 0 else name[:MAX_LEN]) + ext
    return path

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Generate a set of candidate paths and pick one to diversify outcomes while staying seeded
    count = rng.randint(1, 4)
    candidates = [_compose_path(rng) for _ in range(count)]

    # Occasionally include path with nested directories and unique filename
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        candidates.append(_compose_path(rng))

    # Prefer paths likely writable and valid
    # Rank by heuristic: relative paths > /tmp-like > others
    def score(p: str) -> int:
        s = 0
        if p.startswith("./") or (os.name == 'nt' and p.startswith(".\\")):
            s += 3
        if "/tmp" in p or "tmp" in p.lower():
            s += 2
        if any(ext in p for ext in (".xml", ".yml", ".yaml")):
            s += 1
        return s

    candidates.sort(key=score, reverse=True)
    chosen = candidates[0]

    # Ensure bytes are UTF-8
    data = chosen.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
